summary: Shows skipping modules with -Skip when signing. PowerShell content outside collections, like custom scripts or win_powershell code, must be signed manually with Set-AuthenticodeSignature or Set-OpenAuthenticodeSignature and used in a way that doesn't alter it, for example using rstrip=False with the file lookup.
questions: How do I exclude certain modules from App Control signing?
How do I sign my own PowerShell scripts for use with Ansible under WDAC?
Why does my signed script fail when I load it with the file lookup?
Can I sign scripts from Linux for Windows App Control?

answer_card.title: Skipping modules and signing custom scripts
answer_card.answer_md:
Skip modules you don't need:

```powershell
New-AnsiblePowerShellSignature ... -Skip @(
    'ansible.windows.win_dsc'
    'ansible.windows.win_timezone'
)
```

PowerShell that isn't part of a collection (custom scripts, code in `ansible.windows.win_powershell`) must be signed manually: `Set-AuthenticodeSignature` on Windows, or `Set-OpenAuthenticodeSignature` from the `OpenAuthenticode` module on Linux.

Don't let anything change the signed content. `ansible.builtin.script` copies the file as-is, but the `ansible.builtin.file` lookup strips trailing newlines unless you pass `rstrip=False`.
